name: validation-message
purpose: A standalone field message (error, warning, success, or info) for controls that AbsoluteUI does not render itself. It adds its id to the target's aria-describedby and, for errors, sets aria-invalid on the target. AbsoluteUI inputs render the same aui-validation-message markup internally.
whenToUse: Messages for consumer-rendered or third-party controls that should look and behave like AbsoluteUI field messages.
Non-error field feedback such as an availability check result (success, warning, info).
whenNotToUse: AbsoluteUI inputs and Form Field: they render their own messages; use setCustomError() for external errors.
Form-level or page-level errors: use Error Summary.
responsive: Flex row of icon and text; long messages wrap anywhere.
rtl: Follows the document direction; the icon sits at the inline start.
theme: Tone foreground role tokens (color-error-fg, color-warning-fg, color-success-fg, color-info-fg) with a tone icon, so tone is not conveyed by color alone.
security: The message is rendered with textContent and never parsed as HTML. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

budgets.budget: No dedicated performance test; re-renders icon and text on each update

performance.testedScale: Unit tests cover single messages linked to one target.

limitations: Not a live region: a new message is read when the user moves to the target (through aria-describedby), not when it appears.
Every update re-creates the icon element.
No locale option: the message text is consumer-provided.
unsupported: Rendering HTML or links in the message.
Describing more than one target with one message.
antiPatterns: Using a validation message next to an AbsoluteUI input (it duplicates the built-in message).
Relying on tone color alone; keep the message text explicit.
Using tone 'error' for advisory text; it marks the target aria-invalid.
